description: ICS techniques used by CyberAv3ngers, ATT&CK group G1027 (v1.1)
name: CyberAv3ngers (G1027)

techniques.comment: During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) locked out operators by changing the PLC’s IP address.(Citation: Tenable Minnesota Water Utilities)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) locked out operators by changing the PLCs passwords and IP addresses.(Citation: Tenable Minnesota Water Utilities)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) were observed using secure shell ports TCP/22 and common industrial ports (TCP/44818, TCP&UDP/2222, TCP/102, and TCP/502). (Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) disrupted water operations that have included loss of water pressure and flooding.(Citation: Tenable Minnesota Water Utilities)

During the [Unitronics Defacement Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0031), the [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) defaced controllers’ [Human-Machine Interface (HMI)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0002), which prevented multiple entities from being able to operate their devices normally.(Citation: CISA AA23-335A IRGC-Affiliated December 2023)(Citation: CISA Unitronics November 2023)(Citation: Jamie Tarabay and Katrina Manson December 2023)(Citation: Frank Bajak and Marc Levy December 2023) Additionally, the [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) caused a communications failure in a remote pumping station.(Citation: WPXI Aliquippa Water November 2023)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) leveraged existing PLC management protocols through the manufacturer’s engineering tools. These include EtherNet/IP CIP, S7Comm, and UMAS.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) accessed internet-accessible equipment using default credentials.(Citation: Tenable Minnesota Water Utilities)(Citation: Dispel Iran Water Utilities) 

During the [Unitronics Defacement Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0031), the [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) discovered and exploited default credentials found on many Unitronics [Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0003) [Human-Machine Interface (HMI)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0002). For many of these devices, the default password was set to ‘1111’.(Citation: CISA AA23-335A IRGC-Affiliated December 2023)(Citation: CISA Unitronics November 2023)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) accessed internet accessible PLCs that were exposed through cellular gateways across multiple vendors including Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, and Siemens.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [Unitronics Defacement Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0031), the [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) exploited devices connected to the public internet, such as internet connected Unitronics [Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0003) with [Human-Machine Interface (HMI)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0002) and networking equipment such as cellular modems found in OT environments.(Citation: CISA AA23-335A IRGC-Affiliated December 2023)(Citation: Lisa Zahner December 2023)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) degraded operations across at least seven states that resulted in reported incidents, pressure loss and flooding.(Citation: Tenable Minnesota Water Utilities)

During the [Unitronics Defacement Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0031), the [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) caused multiple businesses to halt operations due to the unavailability of the [Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0003) and [Human-Machine Interface (HMI)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0002). These victims covered multiple sectors.(Citation: Jamie Tarabay and Katrina Manson December 2023)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) manipulated process logic, HMI, and SCADA displays. In addition to this, adversaries locked victims out by changing the PLCs management passwords.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [Unitronics Defacement Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0031), the [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) caused multiple businesses to halt operations in their industrial environments, impacting their typical business operations. These victims covered multiple sectors.(Citation: Jamie Tarabay and Katrina Manson December 2023)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) manipulated critical shutdown and alarm logic, which would allow the system to enter unsafe process states without proper notification or protections.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) manipulated process logic, HMI, and SCADA displays, which may disrupt operators view of the system.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [Unitronics Defacement Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0031), the [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) replaced the existing graphic on the [Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0003) [Human-Machine Interface (HMI)](https://attack.mitre.org/assets/A0002) with their own, thereby preventing PLC owners and operators from viewing PLC information on the HMI.(Citation: CISA AA23-335A IRGC-Affiliated December 2023)(Citation: Jamie Tarabay and Katrina Manson December 2023)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) manipulated critical shutdown and alarm logic.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) used manufacturers’ commercial PLC programming software to modify their victim’s running PLC program logic. These include Rockwell Automation’s [Studio Logix 5000 Designer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9054), Schneider Electric’s [EcoStruxure Control Expert](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9056), and Siemens’ [Totally Integrated Automation (TIA) Portal](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9055).(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) used the manufacturers’ commercial PLC programming software to push new configurations to victim hardware. These include Rockwell Automation’s [Studio Logix 5000 Designer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9054), Schneider Electric’s [EcoStruxure Control Expert](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9056), and Siemens’ [Totally Integrated Automation (TIA) Portal](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9055). In these changes, adversaries deleted program logic, removed Add-On Instructions (AOIs) and manipulated alarm logic and HMI screens.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) used the program upload feature to exfiltrate project files from victim PLCs. (Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), one victim reported actors leveraged Dropbear Secure Shell (SSH) software to enable remote access over port 22.(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)

During the [2026 Iranian Water Campaign](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0065), [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) used the manufacturers’ commercial PLC programming and maintenance software to send unauthorized command messages to multiple victim controllers. These include Rockwell Automation’s [Studio Logix 5000 Designer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9054), Schneider Electric’s [EcoStruxure Control Expert](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9056), and Siemens’ [Totally Integrated Automation (TIA) Portal](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9055) .(Citation: CISA-AA26-097A)
